response.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(CAST(rental_rate AS DOUBLE) / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film GROUP BY rating) SELECT rating, avg_ratio, films, avg_ratio - (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) FROM per_rating) AS diff_from_plain_avg FROM per_rating ORDER BY rating;

assumptions.assumption: "The plain average of the five rating-level values" means the unweighted mean of the five per-rating averages computed by the query, not a film-weighted mean.

The division is done in DOUBLE precision. In MySQL, dividing DECIMAL values truncates the result to the dividend's scale plus div_precision_increment (default 4 extra digits), which would violate 'don't round'.
Every film has a non-null rental_rate and replacement_cost (both columns are NOT NULL), and replacement_cost is never zero (the verified minimum is 9.99), so no ratio is NULL or divides by zero.

alternatives.interpretation: Subtract the plain average of the per-film ratios across all films (one unweighted mean over the whole catalogue) instead of the mean of the five rating-level averages.
alternatives.sql: SELECT rating, AVG(CAST(rental_rate AS DOUBLE) / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(CAST(rental_rate AS DOUBLE) / replacement_cost) - (SELECT AVG(CAST(rental_rate AS DOUBLE) / replacement_cost) FROM film) AS diff_from_plain_avg FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY rating;
